questions.question_text: According to Section 1, why is cheating with AI considered a bad idea in high school?

options.text: It makes assignments too easy and boring
It can lead to failing grades, suspension, and missed learning opportunities
It prevents teachers from using AI detection tools
It only affects college students, not high schoolersCorrect Answer: B) It can lead to failing grades, suspension, and missed learning opportunities

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between fair use and plagiarism, as described in Section 2?

options.text: Fair use requires permission for all content, while plagiarism does not
Fair use allows limited use of copyrighted material with conditions, while plagiarism is using others’ work without credit
Fair use applies only to images, while plagiarism applies to text

Fair use is illegal, while plagiarism is acceptable in school projectsCorrect Answer: B) Fair use allows limited use of copyrighted material with conditions, while plagiarism is using others’ work without credit

questions.question_text: Based on Section 3, what is one way high school students can respect privacy when using digital tools for group projects?

options.text: Share classmates’ personal information online to collaborate faster
Post group work on public platforms without asking team members
Ask permission before sharing content involving others and limit access to shared files
Use unsecure apps to store project data for easy accessCorrect Answer: C) Ask permission before sharing content involving others and limit access to shared files

questions.question_text: What does Section 4 highlight as a potential issue with AI tools regarding fairness?

options.text: AI tools are always accurate and unbiased
AI can perpetuate biases from training data, like suggesting stereotypical roles
AI refuses to provide answers on controversial topics
AI only works for certain subjects like math and scienceCorrect Answer: B) AI can perpetuate biases from training data, like suggesting stereotypical roles

questions.question_text: In Section 4, why is it important to fact-check AI output for school projects?

options.text: AI always provides correct information without errors
AI can “hallucinate” facts or give wrong information confidently
AI only works for creative tasks, not factual ones
Fact-checking AI is unnecessary if it sounds convincingCorrect Answer: B) AI can “hallucinate” facts or give wrong information confidently

questions.question_text: What is a key step in creating personal rules for responsible tech use, as discussed in Section 5?

options.text: Rely entirely on school policies without personal reflection
Reflect on your values and set practical boundaries for when and how to use AI
Use AI for all assignments to save time and effort
Avoid using digital tools to prevent ethical dilemmasCorrect Answer: B) Reflect on your values and set practical boundaries for when and how to use AI
